lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Add a short summary that states the product-role target and connects the career story.
items.because: Readers currently have to infer the target and connect the MBA, internship, projects, operations background, and current job.

items.says: Put the Harbor Payments internship before Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The internship ended in 2024, after Crestline ended in 2023, and is more directly relevant to product roles.

items.says: The résumé has limited formal product experience relative to its operations and mechanical experience.
items.because: It shows one product internship and student projects against five years in operations and a recent mechanical role.

items.says: Use a consistent date format throughout.
items.because: A uniform format would look more polished.

items.says: Verify that the contact details are real and clickable in the submitted file.
items.because: The supplied details look like placeholders.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant MBA concentration, coursework, or product-related activity if it merits the space.
items.because: It could strengthen fit for the target role.

items.says: Give concise, truthful context for the current diesel-mechanic role and the career transition.
items.because: The role differs sharply from the product direction suggested by the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Clarify what “under 5 days per job” measures and whether it is a typical result or a target.
Consider whether this marine-service bullet earns its space in a product-focused résumé.
items.because: Its operational-reliability evidence is less relevant than the product work.

items.says: Add a defensible outcome for the maintenance or inspection work, or shorten or remove the bullet.
items.because: It communicates responsibility less clearly than an outcome and may not earn its space for product roles.

items.says: Explain the contribution and causal link between the scorecards and the drop in late deliveries.
items.because: The contract or operating changes that produced the reduction are not clear.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% reduction is relative or a percentage-point change.
Distinguish the slotting redesign, rollout, picker training, and contribution to the result.
items.because: The current phrasing makes those pieces run together.

items.says: Clarify whether the change in forecast error from 18% to 11% is a percentage-point difference or a relative reduction.
Make the main route-planning contribution and its link to the hours saved easier to identify.
items.because: Tool rollout, procedures, training, and vendor negotiations crowd the bullet.

items.says: Specify how the 1,800 annual driver hours saved were measured or estimated.
Clarify what “around a single verification step” means in practice.
Clarify what the onboarding pilot covered.
items.because: The pilot scope helps explain the result.

items.says: Consolidate or distinguish this checkout-test accomplishment from the A/B-test bullet.
items.because: Reporting the same experiment twice can make the short internship look padded.

items.says: Explain what decision the RICE scoring informed or what happened as a result.
items.because: The Reach explanation is more procedural than outcome-focused.

items.says: Distinguish this prioritization work from the merchant-interviews and roadmap bullet.
items.because: The two bullets describe overlapping dispute-roadmap work.

items.says: Distinguish the discovery and business-case work from the RICE prioritization bullet.
items.because: The two bullets describe overlapping dispute-roadmap work.

items.says: Clarify whether you recommended, co-developed, or owned the roadmap decision.
items.because: The stated ownership is hard to judge.

items.says: Remove or distinguish this A/B-test bullet from the checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: It appears to repeat the same test without a clearly distinct contribution.

items.says: Clarify the unit of analysis and the claimed effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: The phrase about reporting the lift as an effect on customers is hard to interpret.

items.says: Clarify how the funded regional expansion relates to the onboarding results.
Avoid implying the presentation alone caused the rollout funding unless that is accurate.
items.because: The causal role of the presentation is not established.

items.says: Verify that “Present” reflects the project’s status and your current involvement.
items.because: It appears alongside a current full-time role.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 means students reached, eligible students, or users.
items.because: The app’s scope is not precise.

items.says: Explain the measurement basis for the 9 tonnes of food redistributed.
items.because: The impact metric needs a clear basis.

items.says: The stated counts do not represent a 150% increase in weekly active users.
items.because: Growth from 400 to 1,150 does not equal 150%.

items.says: State the period covered by the weekly-active-user comparison.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The bullet confuses a percentage-point change with a percent increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the $2.4M is projected or realized savings.
State the assumptions supporting the savings estimate.
Mention the pilot approval only once across the practicum bullets.
items.because: The later bullet repeats the pilot approval given here.

items.says: Use active wording that makes your personal role in the intake work clear.
items.because: The passive construction obscures what you mapped or changed.

items.says: Explain what it means that front-desk staff adopted the changes.
items.because: The outcome is less specific than the other bullets.

items.says: Remove the repeated pilot approval or add distinct evidence about the presentation or stakeholder influence.
items.because: Pilot approval is already mentioned in the first practicum bullet.

items.says: Expand the thin skills section with truthful, relevant product methods and tools.
items.because: It does not show the depth of product analytics and execution demonstrated in the bullets.

items.says: Organize the skill categories to make product methods and tools easier to find.
items.because: “Product” and “Tools” are serviceable but do not fully signal the relevant methods and tools.
